alerts.title: Carbamazepine-DTG interaction lowers DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases DTG concentrations by 30-70% and recommend using valproic acid instead. Carbamazepine was started 2 weeks ago, and the viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence. This interaction is a likely contributor to virologic failure. The patient is already on sodium valproate, making carbamazepine potentially redundant. No alternative cause for the viral load rise is documented.

evidence.recommended_action: Replace carbamazepine with valproic acid or another non-interacting antiepileptic. If carbamazepine cannot be stopped, consider DTG 50 mg twice daily and repeat viral load in 2-3 months.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load requires enhanced adherence plan
alerts.message: Guidelines require that patients on DTG-based ART with VL >50 copies/mL receive enhanced adherence support, have potential side-effects addressed, and repeat VL in 2-3 months. The clinician's plan addresses carbamazepine toxicity but does not document enhanced adherence counselling or a repeat viral load plan. The drug interaction with carbamazepine may itself be the side-effect affecting adherence.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, address carbamazepine-DTG interaction as a potential cause, and schedule repeat viral load in 2-3 months.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatraemia
alerts.message: Carbamazepine level is 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4-12), with symptoms of ataxia, nystagmus, and tremor. Sodium is 128 mmol/L, consistent with carbamazepine-induced SIADH. ALT is mildly elevated at 68 U/L, which may also reflect carbamazepine hepatotoxicity. The plan to reduce the dose is appropriate, but close monitoring of sodium and liver enzymes is needed given the compounding risk of toxicity and hyponatraemia.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose as planned, repeat level, and monitor sodium and ALT. Consider switching to valproic acid to address both toxicity and DTG interaction.
